provision_decisions.note: Rule (17)(a) is verbatim in 1-1907/s31 and states the pre-drafting search duty; see PROV-M014-901 for the proviso the map omitted.
Wording verbatim; the corpus text carries no (b) marker, so the (17)(b)(i) label is a reconstruction of the numbering.
Rule (16)(a) description requirement verbatim, including the district limb the answer relies on.
Rule (16)(b) divided share requirement verbatim; supports the survey step.

Rule (22) verbatim. On its own words the bar is on attesting in an area other than that of the warrant, not on the situation of the land, and rule (29) corroborates that reading by providing for deeds affecting land in another district.
Rule (29) verbatim, but it is triggered by the district in which the notary resides and neither the matter nor the enrichment states his residence; s.9 fixes his office, not his residence.
Rule (6) stamp duty assurance verbatim.
Rule (9) identification verbatim.
s.38(1) true and full consideration verbatim.
s.38A(1) true legal nature of the transaction verbatim; in force from 2024, so applicable at 2025-10.
s.2 warrant specifies area and language, verbatim.
s.9 office within the area of the warrant, verbatim.
s.2(1)(a) of the Prevention of Frauds Ordinance verbatim in the post-2024 consolidated text; correctly held as background.
s.7(1) priority of registered instruments verbatim.
s.13(2) divided portion verbatim.

s.13(5) verbatim, but s.13(5A) and (5B) allow an appeal to the Registrar-General who may reverse a refusal where the description identifies the land with reasonable certainty, so refusal is not the absolute bar the why_relevant states.
s.30(1) priority notice verbatim; the curly quotes in the excerpt normalise to the corpus text.
s.3(1) nullity for want of prior consent verbatim; the coconut reach depends on PROV-M014-022, which is verified.
s.3(4) attachment of the certificate and its recital in the attestation verbatim; this is the direct duty on the notary.

Definition text verbatim, but its operative limb is registration under the Coconut Development Act, No. 46 of 1971, which is not in the corpus; the applicability of the fragmentation control therefore cannot be closed here.
Definition of transfer of ownership verbatim and it does reach any portion of the estate by sale.
20-2005 s.3(1) substitutes throughout the principal enactment and in any other written law; paragraph (c) does replace the words tea or rubber estate, so it reaches both s.3 and s.25.
s.14 preparation of the certificate by the Secretary of the Board verbatim.
Fifty acre ceiling verbatim, but the temporal note misattributes it: Act No. 39 of 1981 s.2 amends only s.3(4) and (5) and leaves the ceiling untouched.
s.5(1) verbatim; Act No. 39 of 1981 s.3 inserts s.5(2) and leaves s.5(1) as enacted.
Added: proviso to rule (17) permitting the parties to dispense with the search in writing.
Added: rule (33), best endeavours to obtain the title deed and endorse it.
Added: s.8(1) of Act No. 2 of 1958, the criteria on which the Board grants consent, including transfers that divide the estate into lots.

added_provisions.reason: The map states the rule (17) search duty without its proviso. The proviso lets the parties authorise the notary in writing to dispense with the search, substituting a duty to write the reference to the previous registration at the head of the deed. A statement of the first pre-drafting step is incomplete without it.

The gold conclusion lists examination of the vendor's title deeds as a step, but no cited provision supported it. Rule (33) is the corpus source for calling for and endorsing the title deed. Added and referenced from CL-M014-Q01-023.

The map treats the Board's certificate as a formality to be produced. Section 8(1)(b) governs a transfer that divides the estate into lots, which is exactly this transaction, and sets the conditions on which consent will or will not be granted. Without it the advice to require the certificate has no account of whether it can be obtained.

question_decisions.note: Authority requirement is right: every step in the answer is traceable to a statute in the corpus and no case law or Roman-Dutch doctrine is needed to state the steps. The question is downgraded on one limb only. The fragmentation consent step, which the map makes indispensable and which the hop count is built on, depends on PROV-M014-020, whose registration limb points to the Coconut Development Act, No. 46 of 1971, absent from the corpus. The notarial duties, the registration description rules and the territorial limit are all verified and would stand on their own if a lawyer decides the fragmentation limb cannot be closed.

disagreements.researcher_position: Polwatta is a coconut estate within s.25 of Act No. 2 of 1958 because the enrichment makes it twelve hectares and registered with the Coconut Cultivation Board, so a prior certificate of consent of the Board is required and the notary must obtain it before drafting.
disagreements.verifier_position: The four hectare limb is met on the enriched facts, but the definition requires the estate to be, or be deemed to be, an estate registered under the Coconut Development Act, No. 46 of 1971. That Act is not in the corpus and registration with the Coconut Cultivation Board is not the same statutory fact. On the corpus alone the control cannot be shown to bite.

disagreements.researcher_position: Rule (22) limits the notary by the place of attestation and the language only, so a Colombo notary may attest a deed for Kurunegala land executed at his Colombo office.
disagreements.verifier_position: The same reading follows from the words of rule (22), and rule (29) corroborates it by providing for deeds that affect land in a district other than the notary's. Recorded not as a contested point but so that a lawyer can confirm that practice does not read rule (22) more widely.

unsupported_claims: CL-M014-Q01-022 asserts the notary must transmit a certified copy to the Kurunegala Registrar of Lands because the land lies outside the district in which he resides, but rule (29) turns on residence and no fact in the matter or the enrichment states where he resides. Marked disputed.

CL-M014-Q01-023 lists examination of the vendor's title deeds as a step with no provision behind it. PROV-M014-902 (rule (33)) has been added and cited; the claim is still marked disputed because it also repeats the consent step that rests on PROV-M014-020.
CL-M014-Q01-008 and CL-M014-Q01-018 rest on the coconut estate definition whose registration limb cannot be checked from the corpus. Both marked disputed.
temporal_issues: PROV-M014-024 temporal note attributes the fifty acre ceiling to Act No. 39 of 1981; that Act's s.2 amends only s.3(4) and (5). The ceiling in the corpus text is the 1972 figure.

The corpus holds Act No. 2 of 1958 as enacted, so ss.3 and 25 still read tea or rubber estate and the coconut reach exists only through 20-2005 s.3(1). The map handles this correctly and flags it, and the substitution is general enough to reach both sections.
No provision in the map relies on an amendment later than the matter reference date. The 2022 and 2024 Notaries amendments are already worked into the consolidated corpus text.
missing_definitions_or_exceptions: Proviso to rule (17): the parties may authorise the notary in writing to dispense with the search. Added as PROV-M014-901.
Registration of Documents Ordinance s.13(5A) and (5B): appeal against a Registrar's refusal, which qualifies PROV-M014-016.
Act No. 2 of 1958 s.8(1)(b): the conditions on which the Board grants consent to a transfer that divides an estate into lots. Added as PROV-M014-903.

Act No. 2 of 1958 s.23A (inserted by 20-2005 s.9): no officer of a local authority may approve a blocking out plan of a coconut estate without a s.14 certificate. Relevant to the survey and plan step and not in the map; not added because the survey step is already supported.
Notaries Ordinance s.31 rule (33): title deed. Added as PROV-M014-902.

The alternative Acts the researcher rejected were checked and the rejections hold: Survey Act No. 17 of 2002 ss.12 and 13 concern deposit and admissibility of plans, and Land (Restrictions on Alienation) Act No. 38 of 2014 bites on foreign transferees. Stamp Duty (Special Provisions) Act No. 12 of 2006 is in the corpus but s.4 does not list a transfer of immovable property as a specified instrument and s.13 leaves such transfers outside its operation, so the researcher's stamp duty gap note is accurate.
case_law_dependence: None. The answer cites no case, and the researcher correctly left out the customary thirty year investigation of title because no corpus provision prescribes it.
enrichment_issues: FACT-M014-Q01-002 says the estate is registered with the Coconut Cultivation Board. The statutory limb is registration under the Coconut Development Act, No. 46 of 1971. The fact does not track the definition it is meant to activate, and the Act that would settle it is outside the corpus. This is the main reason the question is downgraded.

FACT-M014-Q01-001 is marked synthetic_neutral, but making the purchaser a Sri Lankan citizen is what keeps the Land (Restrictions on Alienation) Act out of the answer, so it is closer to decisive than neutral.

No added fact leaks a statute name, a section number or the conclusion. Naming the Coconut Cultivation Board comes close to signposting the fragmentation issue and a lawyer may want it rewritten as an ordinary fact about the estate.
duplicate_or_leak_issues: Provision ids are unique, the indispensable, supporting and background sets are disjoint, and no provision appears twice in a role set. Several provisions share section id 1-1907/s31 but each carries a distinct rule and excerpt, which is unavoidable because the corpus stores s.31 as one body.
The enriched background does not restate the question or the answer.

lawyer_questions: Does registration with the Coconut Cultivation Board satisfy the limb in s.25 of Act No. 2 of 1958 that the estate be, or be deemed to be, an estate registered under the Coconut Development Act, No. 46 of 1971, and is the fragmentation control in practice applied to a sale of a two acre portion of a twelve hectare coconut estate?

Is rule (22) of s.31 read in practice as limiting the notary only by the place of attestation and the language, so that a Colombo notary may draw and attest a deed for Kurunegala land executed at his Colombo office?
Does rule (29) apply on these facts, given that it is expressed by reference to where the notary resides rather than where his warrant or office is?
Should a five mark answer on pre-drafting steps carry the Land Reform Law ceiling check at all, or is it padding that a marker would not expect?
Should the customary thirty year investigation of title be part of the gold answer even though no corpus provision prescribes it?
